tools.name: luma_session_open
tools.title: Open a Luma session
tools.description: Open a session with Luma for one workspace. THE ONLY TOOL THAT CREATES A SESSION — call it once per workspace and pass the session_id it returns to every other tool. workspace_key is optional: omitted, the session opens in your team's shared default workspace, created on first use; re-using a key re-uses that named workspace and its assets. To continue earlier work, find its workspace_key with luma_workspace_list first. End users who must not see each other's assets need a workspace_key each. Everything long-running afterwards is a run on this session: luma_generate_image / luma_generate_video / luma_generate_layering for one media call, luma_session_run_capability for a task one of Luma's capabilities fits, luma_session_send_brief for creative work no capability fits. Every run's outputs land in this workspace with an asset_id any later call can name. Returns a session_id and a resource URI to read.

tools.name: luma_session_run_capability
tools.title: Run a capability
tools.description: Run one of Luma's capabilities on a brief, inside a session you already opened. The session's assistant starts it and relays what the capability says, asks and delivers. Follow the work with luma_session_await, passing the seq this returns as after_seq, and act when it says your_turn or requires_action. Prefer a fitting capability over luma_generate_image / luma_generate_video even when the deliverable is one image or video: a capability plans, generates and judges the task it is built for. Use a generate tool when no capability fits, or the user asks for a particular model. Never substitute a capability that cannot produce what was asked for. Get the slug from luma_capability_list, then use luma_capability_describe. Always pass the user's own words as brief, plus an object matching intake.input_schema as input when present. When one request asks for several independent pieces of work, run a separate capability for each, so each can be stopped or changed on its own. A field in input that takes a file, or a brief, can also name a team-library file by its media: id from luma_library_list_directory. Talk to the user about their work, never about how it runs: say "the request", "the work" or "the result" instead of runs, sessions, apps' internal names, tool names, stages or error codes, and describe a service failure as a temporary problem on our side, without technical detail. A billing or credit failure is not a service failure: tell the user its message as given, and never say work was created or charged when it was not. Asset ids are handles for later tool calls; show one only when the user needs to point at a specific asset.

tools.title: Send a brief
tools.description: Brief a session that is already open. Use it for multi-image or multi-shot requests no capability in luma_capability_list fits (a story in three images, a series that shares characters or a style): describe the whole set in one brief. Several images, or one image in several sizes or formats, often fit a capability; run that with luma_session_run_capability instead. The session's agent has the message history and any ref_artifacts, so a follow-up can revise, extend or re-cut an earlier output by referring to it, and can answer a clarification it asked for. Within what your session grant allows, it reaches the creative actions across the granted models — generating, editing, upscaling, reframing, trimming and stitching clips together, and audio: music, sound effects, voiceover, and lip-syncing a video to a voice track. For a single image or clip that no capability fits, call luma_generate_image or luma_generate_video directly. Send every user reply this way, including an answer to a question a capability asked: the assistant forwards it. Each brief runs an agent turn and bills to the session; one sent while a turn runs is taken after it. Returns at once; follow the work with luma_session_await, passing the seq this returns as after_seq, or keep the after_seq of a wait that answered working. A brief sent to a completed or expired session is refused with 409. Talk to the user about their work, never about how it runs: say "the request", "the work" or "the result" instead of runs, sessions, apps' internal names, tool names, stages or error codes, and describe a service failure as a temporary problem on our side, without technical detail. A billing or credit failure is not a service failure: tell the user its message as given, and never say work was created or charged when it was not. Asset ids are handles for later tool calls; show one only when the user needs to point at a specific asset.

tools.description: THE way to follow a session after luma_session_send_brief, luma_session_run_capability or luma_run_respond. Each call holds up to about 50 s. While the work goes on it answers status working with a short status_line you may show and nothing else: call it again right away with the same after_seq. Only your_turn, requires_action or ended carry what happened since after_seq (the assistant's messages, results with asset ids): tell the user, then pass next_after_seq next time; when has_more is true, call again with it to read the rest before acting. requires_action lists waiting items: a review or request is the user's decision: first show them the item's show assets with luma_workspace_view_asset, then ask them, fill answer_format from their choice and answer with luma_run_respond. When stop_reason is error, failure says what went wrong: tell the user failure.message. On your_turn the session stays open, so offer to try again when failure.retryable is true; on ended it cannot continue. When this host has luma_workspace_view_asset, call it with up to 4 image and video asset ids the events delivered to display them in this host's viewer, then again with the next ids until all are shown. When luma_session_await returns media_display=call_view_asset, call luma_workspace_view_asset with up to 4 of the waiting items' show assets at a time before asking the user. Talk to the user about their work, never about how it runs: say "the request", "the work" or "the result" instead of runs, sessions, apps' internal names, tool names, stages or error codes, and describe a service failure as a temporary problem on our side, without technical detail. A billing or credit failure is not a service failure: tell the user its message as given, and never say work was created or charged when it was not. Asset ids are handles for later tool calls; show one only when the user needs to point at a specific asset.

tools.name: luma_generate_image
tools.title: Generate an image
tools.description: Create or edit one still image in a session you already opened. Use it for a hero shot, a product still, a poster frame, a thumbnail, or a variation on an image the workspace already holds (type='image_edit', the asset_id in source — editing never changes the original). Name the model by an image row's id from luma_model_list. When the user names no model, make a new image with openai_gpt_image_2_5_sunburst while luma_model_list lists it, unless another model's strengths and luma_model_describe guidance fit the request better. A third-party model takes prompt, aspect_ratio, medias and the parameters luma_model_describe lists; source and image_ref are for a model luma_model_describe lists no parameters and no media roles for. It need not wait for other work on the session to finish. Returns a run_id; call luma_run_await with it, and the outputs come back with an asset_id you can pass to any later call. NOT for video of any kind — use luma_generate_video; NOT for splitting an image into layers — use luma_generate_layering. Check luma_capability_list first: when a capability fits the task, run it with luma_session_run_capability, even for one image. Use this tool when none fits, or the user asks for a particular model.

url.description: A publicly reachable media URL. Not for reference_audio, which takes an asset_id or file_id.

asset_id.title: Asset Id

role.description: What the media is to the model: reference (a reference image), start_frame, end_frame, keyframe (an image on the model's keyframe timeline, spaced evenly from the first frame to the last in the order sent), reference_video or reference_audio. A role the model does not take is refused, naming the roles it takes.

RunMediaRef.description:
A ``MediaRef`` with the workspace arm — runs only.

A run writes into the session's workspace, so "an asset the workspace
already holds" means something there. ``/v1/generations`` has no session
and no workspace to resolve against, which is why this is a subclass and
not a sixth arm on ``MediaRef``: the base class is what the published SDK
renders, and an arm no sessionless caller can use does not belong in it.

url.description: Publicly accessible image or video URL
url.title: Url

media_type.description: MIME type (e.g. image/jpeg, video/mp4). Required with ``data``. Required with ``url`` when used as ``body.source`` on ``type=video_edit`` / ``type=video_reframe`` (the route uses the prefix to dispatch the image vs video ingest path; an absent or non-``video/*`` value is rejected). Optional with ``url`` on image positions — content-type is sniffed from the response.

generation_id.description: UUID of a prior generation owned by the same caller. The route resolves that generation's output artifact as input — chain reference. Used on ``body.source`` (chained ``image_edit`` off a prior image output; chained ``video_edit`` / ``video_reframe`` off a prior video output) and on ``video.start_frame`` / ``video.end_frame`` (extend forward / backward). Cross-client lookups collapse to 404 ``file_not_found`` shape so partners can't enumerate other partners' UUIDs. Chained outputs stay in the source generation's workspace.

Valid at every ref position. Unlike ``generation_id`` the source need not be a completed generation, and editing one never changes it: the result is a new asset. Cross-workspace and cross-team lookups answer 404, the same shape a missing asset does. Takes an artifact in this session's workspace or a team-library file; spelled as a bare id or `kind:id`, a library file always as media:<id>; one id only, never a joined pair.

RunVideoControls.description: ``VideoControls`` whose every frame slot carries the workspace arm.

resolution.description: Output resolution. Defaults to 720p when omitted. 360p (draft tier) is accepted on type=video, video_edit, and video_reframe (SDR only). With hdr=true on type=video, only 720p / 1080p are accepted, so 360p is SDR-only there.
resolution.title: Resolution

duration.description: Video duration. Defaults to 5s when omitted. With hdr=true on type=video, only 5s is accepted.
duration.title: Duration

hdr.description: Generate HDR video. On type=video the HDR variant accepts only resolution 720p/1080p, duration 5s, and no loop; on type=video_edit there are no narrower constraints.
hdr.title: Hdr

exr_export.description: Export EXR alongside the MP4 (HDR-only, professional color grading). Requires hdr=true.
exr_export.title: Exr Export

png_export.description: Export a .zip of PNG frames alongside the MP4. Requires hdr=false (SDR only).
png_export.title: Png Export

loop.description: Generate a seamlessly looping video (type=video only). 10s + loop is unsupported, and loop is not valid with hdr=true.
loop.title: Loop

start_frame.description: First frame of the video. On type=video, turns text-to-video into image-to-video (start-pinned). On type=video_edit, the single guide frame. Provide via url or inline base64 data — same shape as ``source``.

end_frame.description: Last frame of the video (type=video only; interpolates between start_frame and end_frame when both are set).

guide_frame.description: Reframe guide frame (type=video_reframe only) — an image that styles the AI-outpainted areas of the new canvas. Optional; omit to let the model derive the expanded content from the source video and prompt alone. Image MIMEs only, and ``generation_id`` is not accepted at this position: provide ``url``, inline base64 ``data`` + ``media_type``, or a ``file_id``. Distinct from ``start_frame``, which is rejected on ``type=video_reframe``.

keyframes.description: Image-to-video guide frames (type=video only), each pinned to an output-frame position via the parallel ``keyframe_indexes``. 1–64 anchors: a single anchor is a valid start-pinned i2v through the modern Ray 3.2 create path (an alternate to ``start_frame``), and any count up to 64 places guide frames at arbitrary positions. Unlike ``start_frame`` / ``end_frame`` (the legacy ≤2-frame surface), this routes to the full Ray 3.2 path — arbitrary positions, 10s durations, and HDR. Mutually exclusive with ``start_frame`` / ``end_frame`` / ``loop``. Each entry takes the same MediaRef shape as ``source`` / ``image_ref[]``. For video-to-video keyframes (anchored to a source video's grid) use ``video.edit.keyframes`` on ``type=video_edit`` instead.
keyframes.title: Keyframes

keyframe_indexes.description: Parallel list of non-negative, unique output-frame positions where each ``keyframes[i]`` is anchored, in the duration×24fps grid (5s → 0..120, 10s → 0..240). Must match ``keyframes`` in length.
keyframe_indexes.title: Keyframe Indexes

edit.description: Video-edit (video-to-video) controls — only valid for type=video_edit.

source_position.description: Normalized source rect inside the output canvas — only valid for ``type=video_reframe``. Each field is 0..1 with width and height allowed up to 2.0 (source can bleed off-canvas). Drives the AI's crop of the source video. Omit to let the model pick its own default centered-fit crop.

RunVideoControls.title: RunVideoControls

RunVideoEditControls.description: ``VideoEditControls`` whose keyframes carry the workspace arm.

strength.description: Preservation-vs-reimagination preset. 'adhere_*' preserves the source closely; 'flex_*' is balanced (default flex_2); 'reimagine_*' grants more creative freedom. Higher numbers within each tier = stronger effect. Supplying it implies manual mode (auto_controls=false) unless auto_controls is explicitly set.
strength.title: Strength

auto_controls.description: When true (the default behavior), the model auto-derives the per-signal control schedule from the source video, bypassing strength / controls. When omitted, supplying 'strength' or 'controls' implies manual mode. Setting auto_controls=true together with 'controls' is rejected.
auto_controls.title: Auto Controls

controls.description: Per-signal manual conditioning overrides (pose, depth, normals, trajectory, face). Supplying this switches the edit to manual mode.

keyframes.description: Multi-anchor guide-frame images at arbitrary source-frame positions (parallel with ``keyframe_indexes``). Up to 64 anchors. Mutually exclusive with ``video.start_frame`` (the single-anchor case). Each entry takes the same MediaRef shape as ``source`` / ``image_ref[]``.
keyframes.title: Keyframes

keyframe_indexes.description: Parallel list of non-negative, unique frame positions in the source video's frame grid where each ``keyframes[i]`` is anchored. Must match ``keyframes`` in length.

SourcePosition.description:
Normalized source rect inside the output canvas for video_reframe.

All fields are dimensionless ratios relative to the output canvas:
``x_norm`` and ``y_norm`` are 0..1 (the source's top-left within
the canvas); ``w_norm`` and ``h_norm`` are 0..2.0 (the source can
extend past the canvas edges, in which case the AI outpaints the
visible portion only).

tools.description: How many credits are left and which Luma team this connection uses, with the credits that team used in the current billing period. Pass session_id instead for the credits a session and everything spawned under it used, by part of the work, each named in words you can show the user; planning the work is the assistant's own model use, not a render, so never report it as a render charge. Pass asset_ids for the final charge of the job that made each generated image or video, and the total; asset_ids needs exactly one of session_id or workspace_id, naming the workspace that holds them. An asset reads credits null when its job has no final per-asset charge, because it is still running or its session bills as a whole; read that work with luma_usage(session_id). The team-wide answer is not available on a connection that declared a partner tenant. Talk to the user about their work, never about how it runs: say "the request", "the work" or "the result" instead of runs, sessions, apps' internal names, tool names, stages or error codes, and describe a service failure as a temporary problem on our side, without technical detail. A billing or credit failure is not a service failure: tell the user its message as given, and never say work was created or charged when it was not. Asset ids are handles for later tool calls; show one only when the user needs to point at a specific asset.
